/**
 * Build a lookup map from file path → batchIndex across all batches (code +
 * non-code). Used to resolve cross-batch neighbor references in neighborMap.
 */
function buildBatchOfMap(allBatches) {
  const m = new Map();
  for (const b of allBatches) {
    for (const f of b.files) m.set(f.path, b.batchIndex);
  }
  return m;
}

function normalizeRelativePathForMatch(pathText) {
  return pathText
    .trim()
    .replace(/\\/g, '/')
    .replace(/^\.\/+/, '')
    .replace(/\/+/g, '/');
}

// ECMAScript string comparison uses a stable UTF-16 code-unit order and does
// not depend on the host locale or ICU version.
function comparePaths(a, b) {
  if (a === b) return 0;
  return a < b ? -1 : 1;
}

/**
 * Returns Map<path, communityId> via Louvain. May throw — caller must catch
 * and fall back if it does. Honors UA_COMPUTE_BATCHES_FORCE_LOUVAIN_THROW=1
 * to allow tests to exercise the fallback path.
 */
function runLouvain(codeFiles, importMap) {
  if (process.env.UA_COMPUTE_BATCHES_FORCE_LOUVAIN_THROW === '1') {
    throw new Error('forced throw via UA_COMPUTE_BATCHES_FORCE_LOUVAIN_THROW');
  }
  const g = new Graph({ type: 'undirected', allowSelfLoops: false });
  const sortedCodePaths = codeFiles.map(f => f.path).sort(comparePaths);
  for (const path of sortedCodePaths) g.addNode(path);
  const sortedImports = Object.entries(importMap)
    .sort(([a], [b]) => comparePaths(a, b));
  for (const [src, targets] of sortedImports) {
    if (!g.hasNode(src)) continue;
    for (const tgt of [...targets].sort(comparePaths)) {
      if (!g.hasNode(tgt) || src === tgt || g.hasEdge(src, tgt)) continue;
      g.addEdge(src, tgt);
    }
  }
  const cs = louvain(g, { randomWalk: false });  // { nodeId: communityId }
  return new Map(Object.entries(cs));
}

/**
 * Returns Map<path, communityId> via alphabetical chunking of `batchSize`
 * files per batch. Deterministic, used as fallback when Louvain fails.
 */
function countBasedAssignment(codeFiles, batchSize = 12) {
  const out = new Map();
  const sorted = [...codeFiles].map(f => f.path).sort();
  for (let i = 0; i < sorted.length; i++) {
    out.set(sorted[i], `count_${Math.floor(i / batchSize)}`);
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * Pool small mergeable batches into "misc" batches to reduce dispatch overhead.
 * Preserves semantic groupings (non-code Groups A-D, marked `mergeable=false`)
 * regardless of size; only merges code Louvain singletons / orphans and
 * Group E parent-dir batches that fall below MIN_BATCH_SIZE.
 *
 * On a 314-file microservices-demo run, vanilla Louvain produced 87 singleton
 * communities → 87 dispatch tasks of size 1. This pass collapses them into
 * ceil(N / MAX_MERGE_TARGET) misc batches, drastically cutting orchestration
 * overhead while leaving the high-modularity communities untouched.
 *
 * Returns the rewritten batch list with reassigned batchIndex (1-based,
 * keepers first preserving their relative order, misc batches appended).
 */
function mergeSmallBatches(bareBatches) {
  // MIN_BATCH_SIZE=3: below this, file-analyzer dispatch overhead (subagent
  // spin-up, prompt setup) dwarfs the per-file analysis cost — not worth a
  // standalone batch.
  const MIN_BATCH_SIZE = 3;
  // MAX_MERGE_TARGET=25: stays below MAX_COMMUNITY_SIZE=35 so the misc-batch
  // agent retains headroom for neighborMap context without overflowing.
  const MAX_MERGE_TARGET = 25;

  const keepers = [];
  const smallMergeable = [];
  for (const b of bareBatches) {
    if (b.mergeable && b.files.length < MIN_BATCH_SIZE) {
      smallMergeable.push(b);
    } else {
      keepers.push(b);
    }
  }

  if (smallMergeable.length === 0) {
    // Nothing to merge — strip mergeable flag and renumber for cleanliness.
    return keepers.map((b, i) => ({
      batchIndex: i + 1,
      files: b.files,
    }));
  }

  // Pool and sort deterministically by path so repeated runs match byte-for-byte.
  const pooledFiles = smallMergeable
    .flatMap(b => b.files)
    .sort((a, b) => comparePaths(a.path, b.path));

  const miscBatches = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < pooledFiles.length; i += MAX_MERGE_TARGET) {
    miscBatches.push({ files: pooledFiles.slice(i, i + MAX_MERGE_TARGET) });
  }

  // Use `Info:` rather than `Warning:` — singleton consolidation is a
  // routine optimization, not a fallback/degrade path. Per
  // [[feedback_visible_warnings]] only fallbacks should bubble as Warning:
  // to the Phase 7 final report. Real warnings would get drowned out if
  // every normal Louvain run with singletons (i.e. almost every run) added
  // a Warning: line.
  process.stderr.write(
    `Info: compute-batches: merged ${smallMergeable.length} small batches ` +
    `(${pooledFiles.length} files) into ${miscBatches.length} misc batches ` +
    `— singletons and orphans consolidated\n`,
  );

  const final = [...keepers, ...miscBatches];
  return final.map((b, i) => ({
    batchIndex: i + 1,
    files: b.files,
  }));
}

// ── Main: load → Louvain (or count-fallback) → enrich → write batches.json ─
async function main() {
  const projectRoot = process.argv[2];
  if (!projectRoot) {
    process.stderr.write(
      'Usage: node compute-batches.mjs <project-root> [--changed-files=<path>] ' +
      '[--scan-result=<path>] [--output=<path>]\n',
    );
    process.exit(1);
  }

  const helperOptions = new Map();
  for (const arg of process.argv.slice(3)) {
    const match = arg.match(/^--(changed-files|scan-result|output)=(.+)$/);
    if (!match) {
      process.stderr.write(`Error: compute-batches: invalid option: ${arg}\n`);
      process.exit(1);
    }
    const [, optionName, optionValue] = match;
    if (helperOptions.has(optionName)) {
      process.stderr.write(`Error: compute-batches: duplicate option: --${optionName}\n`);
      process.exit(1);
    }
    helperOptions.set(optionName, optionValue);
  }

  let changedFiles = null;
  const changedFilesPath = helperOptions.get('changed-files');
  if (changedFilesPath) {
    let content;
    try {
      content = readFileSync(changedFilesPath, 'utf-8');
    } catch (err) {
      process.stderr.write(
        `Error: compute-batches: --changed-files path not readable: ${changedFilesPath} ` +
        `(${err.message})\n`,
      );
      process.exit(1);
    }
    const lines = content
      .split('\n')
      .map(normalizeRelativePathForMatch)
      .filter(Boolean);
    changedFiles = new Set(lines);
  }

  const scanResultValue = helperOptions.get('scan-result');
  const outputValue = helperOptions.get('output');
  const scanResultPath = scanResultValue ? resolve(scanResultValue) : null;
  const outputPath = outputValue ? resolve(outputValue) : null;

  const uaDir = resolveUaDir(projectRoot);
  const scanPath = scanResultPath ?? join(uaDir, 'intermediate', 'scan-result.json');
  if (!existsSync(scanPath)) {
    process.stderr.write(`Error: scan-result.json not found at ${scanPath}\n`);
    process.exit(1);
  }

  const scan = JSON.parse(readFileSync(scanPath, 'utf-8'));
  const files = scan.files || [];
  const codeFiles = files.filter(f => f.fileCategory === 'code');
  const nonCodeFiles = files.filter(f => f.fileCategory !== 'code');
  const importMap = scan.importMap || {};

  process.stderr.write(`Loaded ${files.length} files (${codeFiles.length} code).\n`);

  const exportsByPath = await extractExports(projectRoot, codeFiles);

  let algorithm = 'louvain';
  let perFileCommunity;
  try {
    perFileCommunity = runLouvain(codeFiles, importMap);
  } catch (err) {
    process.stderr.write(
      `Warning: compute-batches: Louvain failed (${err.message}) ` +
      `— falling back to count-based grouping (12 files/batch) ` +
      `— module semantic boundaries lost\n`,
    );
    perFileCommunity = countBasedAssignment(codeFiles, 12);
    algorithm = 'count-fallback';
  }

  // Group files by community id
  const filesByCommunity = new Map();
  for (const [path, cid] of perFileCommunity) {
    if (!filesByCommunity.has(cid)) filesByCommunity.set(cid, []);
    filesByCommunity.get(cid).push(path);
  }

  // Size enforcement only on louvain output. count-fallback already chunked.
  const MAX_COMMUNITY_SIZE = 35;
  const splitCommunities = new Map();
  let nextSyntheticId = 0;
  if (algorithm === 'louvain') {
    for (const [cid, paths] of filesByCommunity) {
      if (paths.length <= MAX_COMMUNITY_SIZE) {
        splitCommunities.set(cid, paths);
        continue;
      }
      process.stderr.write(
        `Warning: compute-batches: community size ${paths.length} > max ${MAX_COMMUNITY_SIZE} ` +
        `— splitting via alphabetical chunking — modularity may decrease\n`,
      );
      const sorted = [...paths].sort();
      const parts = Math.ceil(paths.length / MAX_COMMUNITY_SIZE);
      const perPart = Math.ceil(paths.length / parts);
      for (let i = 0; i < parts; i++) {
        const slice = sorted.slice(i * perPart, (i + 1) * perPart);
        const synthId = `__split_${cid}_${nextSyntheticId++}`;
        splitCommunities.set(synthId, slice);
      }
    }
  } else {
    for (const [cid, paths] of filesByCommunity) splitCommunities.set(cid, paths);
  }

  // Sort communities by size desc, then by min-path asc for determinism
  const sortedCommunities = [...splitCommunities.entries()]
    .sort((a, b) => {
      if (b[1].length !== a[1].length) return b[1].length - a[1].length;
      const minA = [...a[1]].sort()[0];
      const minB = [...b[1]].sort()[0];
      return comparePaths(minA, minB);
    });

  // Build per-batch file list with full file metadata from scan
  const fileMetaByPath = new Map(files.map(f => [f.path, f]));
  // Safe: every path in a community is a graph node, and graph nodes are a
  // subset of files (see addNode loop above). fileMetaByPath.get() can
  // never return undefined here.

  // First-pass: assemble bare batches (no batchImportData/neighborMap yet).
  // All Louvain communities are mergeable=true so the merge-small pass can
  // collapse singletons / 2-file orphans. Non-code groups carry per-group
  // mergeable flags from buildNonCodeBatches (false for semantic Groups A-D,
  // true for Group E catch-all).
  const codeBatchObjsBare = sortedCommunities.map(([, paths], idx) => ({
    batchIndex: idx + 1,
    files: paths.sort().map(p => fileMetaByPath.get(p)),
    mergeable: true,
  }));
  const nonCodeGroups = buildNonCodeBatches(nonCodeFiles);
  const nonCodeBatchObjsBare = nonCodeGroups.map((g, i) => ({
    batchIndex: codeBatchObjsBare.length + i + 1,
    files: g.files,
    mergeable: g.mergeable,
  }));
  const bareBatches = [...codeBatchObjsBare, ...nonCodeBatchObjsBare];
  const mergedBareBatches = mergeSmallBatches(bareBatches);
  const batchOf = buildBatchOfMap(mergedBareBatches);

  // Build reverse import map: target → [sources that import target]
  const reverseImportMap = new Map();
  for (const [src, targets] of Object.entries(importMap)) {
    for (const tgt of targets) {
      if (!reverseImportMap.has(tgt)) reverseImportMap.set(tgt, []);
      reverseImportMap.get(tgt).push(src);
    }
  }

  // Compute neighbor degree (number of import relations) per path, used for
  // truncation when neighborMap[file] has > MAX_NEIGHBORS entries.
  const NEIGHBOR_DEGREE = new Map();
  for (const f of codeFiles) {
    const outDeg = (importMap[f.path] || []).length;
    const inDeg = (reverseImportMap.get(f.path) || []).length;
    NEIGHBOR_DEGREE.set(f.path, outDeg + inDeg);
  }

  const MAX_NEIGHBORS = 50;

  // Second-pass: enrich each batch with batchImportData + neighborMap.
  // `analysisFiles` is usually the full batch. In --changed-files mode, it is
  // only the changed target set, while batchOf remains the full-graph lookup.
  const buildBatchPayload = (b, analysisFiles = b.files) => {
    const analysisPaths = new Set(analysisFiles.map(f => f.path));
    const batchImportData = {};
    const neighborMap = {};
    for (const f of analysisFiles) {
      batchImportData[f.path] = (importMap[f.path] || []).slice();

      // 1-hop neighbors: imports out + imported-by in, excluding files already
      // emitted for analysis in this payload.
      // Note on truncation: we measure "popularity" by total raw 1-hop neighbor
      // count (rawCount), not kept.length. A widely-imported hub like a logger
      // module may have N>50 inbound imports but, after Louvain + size
      // enforcement, only some land in other batches — kept.length can be < 50
      // while the file is still a high-degree hub whose missing relationships
      // matter for downstream cross-batch edge confidence. Warning on rawCount
      // surfaces this; truncation on kept ensures the JSON stays bounded.
      const outNeighbors = importMap[f.path] || [];
      const inNeighbors = reverseImportMap.get(f.path) || [];
      const all = new Set([...outNeighbors, ...inNeighbors]);
      const rawCount = all.size;
      const filtered = [...all].filter(p => batchOf.has(p) && !analysisPaths.has(p));

      let kept = filtered.map(p => ({
        path: p,
        batchIndex: batchOf.get(p),
        symbols: exportsByPath.get(p) || [],
      }));

      if (rawCount > MAX_NEIGHBORS) {
        kept.sort((a, b2) => (NEIGHBOR_DEGREE.get(b2.path) || 0)
                            - (NEIGHBOR_DEGREE.get(a.path) || 0)
                            || comparePaths(a.path, b2.path));  // deterministic tiebreak
        const beforeSlice = kept.length;
        kept = kept.slice(0, MAX_NEIGHBORS);
        process.stderr.write(
          `Warning: compute-batches: neighborMap for ${f.path} has high 1-hop degree ${rawCount} ` +
          `— exceeds soft cap of ${MAX_NEIGHBORS} — keeping top ${kept.length} cross-batch entries ` +
          `(${beforeSlice - kept.length} dropped by degree sort)\n`,
        );
      }

      if (kept.length) neighborMap[f.path] = kept;
    }
    return { batchIndex: b.batchIndex, files: analysisFiles, batchImportData, neighborMap };
  };

  const batches = mergedBareBatches.map(b => buildBatchPayload(b));

  let finalBatches = batches;
  if (changedFiles) {
    finalBatches = mergedBareBatches
      .map(b => {
        const changedBatchFiles = b.files.filter(f =>
          changedFiles.has(normalizeRelativePathForMatch(f.path)));
        if (changedBatchFiles.length === 0) return null;
        return buildBatchPayload(b, changedBatchFiles);
      })
      .filter(Boolean);
    // batchIndex on filtered batches retains the full-graph assignment
    // (the design says neighborMap should still reference unchanged files'
    // full-graph batchIndex). No renumbering.
  }

  // Note: under --changed-files mode, totalFiles is the FULL project file
  // count (unchanged from the input scan) while totalBatches reflects only
  // the filtered set written to disk. batchIndex values on the kept batches
  // preserve the full-graph assignment so neighborMap references resolve.
  const output = {
    schemaVersion: 1,
    algorithm,
    totalFiles: scan.files.length,
    totalBatches: finalBatches.length,
    exportsByPath: Object.fromEntries(exportsByPath),
    batches: finalBatches,
  };

  const outPath = outputPath ?? join(uaDir, 'intermediate', 'batches.json');
  mkdirSync(dirname(outPath), { recursive: true });
  writeFileSync(outPath, JSON.stringify(output, null, 2), 'utf-8');
  const batchSizes = finalBatches.map(b => b.files.length);
  const maxSize = batchSizes.length ? Math.max(...batchSizes) : 0;
  const minSize = batchSizes.length ? Math.min(...batchSizes) : 0;
  process.stderr.write(
    `Wrote ${finalBatches.length} batches (sizes: max=${maxSize}, min=${minSize}) to ${outPath}\n`,
  );
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Run only when executed directly as a CLI; importing the module (e.g. from
// tests) must not trigger main().
//
// Canonicalize both sides through realpathSync. Node ESM resolves
// import.meta.url through symlinks but pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]) preserves
// them, so a raw equality check silently no-ops when the script is invoked via
// a symlinked plugin install path (the default in Claude Code / Copilot CLI
// caches). See GitHub issue #162.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
function isCliEntry() {
  if (!process.argv[1]) return false;
  try {
    const modulePath = realpathSync(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
    const argvPath = realpathSync(process.argv[1]);
    return modulePath === argvPath;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

if (isCliEntry()) {
  try {
    await main();
  } catch (err) {
    process.stderr.write(`compute-batches.mjs failed: ${err.message}\n${err.stack}\n`);
    process.exit(1);
  }

/**
 * extract-structure.mjs
 *
 * Deterministic structural extraction script for the file-analyzer agent.
 * Uses PluginRegistry (TreeSitterPlugin + non-code parsers) from @understand-anything/core
 * to replace the LLM-generated throwaway regex scripts in Phase 1.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   node extract-structure.mjs <input.json> <output.json>
 *
 * Input JSON:
 *   { projectRoot, batchFiles: [{path, language, sizeLines, fileCategory}], batchImportData }
 *
 * Output JSON:
 *   { scriptCompleted, filesAnalyzed, filesSkipped, results: [...] }

import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { dirname, resolve, join } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { existsSync, readFileSync, realpathSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import {
  analyzeFileWithOutcomes,
  buildResult as buildExtractResult,
} from './extract-structure-result.mjs';

export {
  analyzeFileWithOutcomes,
  buildResult,
} from './extract-structure-result.mjs';

const __dirname = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
// skills/understand/ -> plugin root is two dirs up
const pluginRoot = resolve(__dirname, '../..');
const require = createRequire(resolve(pluginRoot, 'package.json'));

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Resolve @understand-anything/core
//
// Node ESM dynamic import() requires a file:// URL on Windows; passing a raw
// absolute path like "C:\..." throws ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME because the
// loader parses "C:" as a URL scheme. Wrap both resolutions in pathToFileURL().
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
let core;
try {
  core = await import(pathToFileURL(require.resolve('@understand-anything/core')).href);
} catch {
  // Fallback: direct path for installed plugin cache layouts
  core = await import(pathToFileURL(resolve(pluginRoot, 'packages/core/dist/index.js')).href);
}

const { TreeSitterPlugin, PluginRegistry, builtinLanguageConfigs, registerAllParsers } = core;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Main
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
async function main() {
  const [,, inputPath, outputPath] = process.argv;
  if (!inputPath || !outputPath) {
    process.stderr.write('Usage: node extract-structure.mjs <input.json> <output.json>\n');
    process.exit(1);
  }

  // Read input
  const inputRaw = readFileSync(inputPath, 'utf-8');
  const input = JSON.parse(inputRaw);
  const { projectRoot, batchFiles, batchImportData } = input;

  if (!projectRoot || !Array.isArray(batchFiles)) {
    throw new Error('Invalid input: must contain projectRoot and batchFiles array');
  }

  // Create tree-sitter plugin with all configs that have WASM grammars
  const tsConfigs = builtinLanguageConfigs.filter(c => c.treeSitter);
  const tsPlugin = new TreeSitterPlugin(tsConfigs);
  await tsPlugin.init();

  // Create registry and register tree-sitter + all non-code parsers
  const registry = new PluginRegistry();
  registry.register(tsPlugin);
  registerAllParsers(registry);

  const results = [];
  const filesSkipped = [];
  const analysisOutcomes = {
    structure: { succeeded: 0, failed: 0 },
    callGraph: { succeeded: 0, failed: 0, skipped: 0 },
  };

  for (const file of batchFiles) {
    const absolutePath = join(projectRoot, file.path);

    // Read file content
    let content;
    try {
      content = readFileSync(absolutePath, 'utf-8');
    } catch {
      filesSkipped.push(file.path);
      continue;
    }

    // Line counts. POSIX text files end in a trailing newline, which makes
    // `split('\n')` produce one extra empty element. Match `wc -l` semantics
    // (used by the project scanner for `sizeLines`) so the two counts agree.
    const lines = content.split('\n');
    const totalLines = content.endsWith('\n') ? Math.max(0, lines.length - 1) : lines.length;
    const nonEmptyLines = lines.filter(l => l.trim().length > 0).length;

    const { analysis, callGraph, structureOutcome, callGraphOutcome } =
      analyzeFileWithOutcomes(registry, file, content);

    if (structureOutcome === 'skipped') {
      filesSkipped.push(file.path);
      continue;
    }

    analysisOutcomes.structure[structureOutcome] += 1;
    analysisOutcomes.callGraph[callGraphOutcome] += 1;

    // Build result object
    const result = buildExtractResult(file, totalLines, nonEmptyLines, analysis, callGraph, batchImportData);
    results.push(result);
  }

  // Write output
  const output = {
    scriptCompleted: true,
    filesAnalyzed: results.length,
    filesSkipped,
    analysisOutcomes,
    results,
  };

  writeFileSync(outputPath, JSON.stringify(output, null, 2), 'utf-8');

  if (!existsSync(outputPath)) {
    throw new Error(`output file missing after write: ${outputPath}`);
  }
}

// Run only when executed directly as a CLI; importing the module (e.g. from
// tests) must not trigger main().
//
// Canonicalize both sides through realpathSync. Node ESM resolves
// import.meta.url through symlinks but pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]) preserves
// them, so a raw equality check silently no-ops when the script is invoked via
// a symlinked plugin install path (the default in Claude Code / Copilot CLI
// caches). See GitHub issue #162.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
function isCliEntry() {
  if (!process.argv[1]) return false;
  try {
    const modulePath = realpathSync(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
    const argvPath = realpathSync(process.argv[1]);
    return modulePath === argvPath;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

if (isCliEntry()) {
  try {
    await main();
  } catch (err) {
    process.stderr.write(`extract-structure.mjs failed: ${err.message}\n${err.stack}\n`);
    process.exit(1);
  }

1: #!/usr/bin/env node
2: /**
3:  * extract-import-map.mjs
4:  *
5:  * Deterministic import resolution script for the project-scanner agent.
6:  * Uses PluginRegistry (TreeSitterPlugin + non-code parsers) from
7:  * @understand-anything/core to extract raw import paths via tree-sitter,
8:  * then applies language-specific resolution rules to map them to
9:  * project-internal file paths.
10:  *
11:  * Replaces the LLM-written prose import resolver in agents/project-scanner.md
12:  * (the prose previously described patterns by language; runtime LLMs produced
13:  * inconsistent, regex-only scripts with sparse coverage).
14:  *
15:  * Usage:
16:  *   node extract-import-map.mjs <input.json> <output.json>
17:  *
18:  * Input JSON:
19:  *   {
20:  *     projectRoot: <abs-path>,
21:  *     files: [{ path, language, fileCategory }, ...]
22:  *   }
23:  *
24:  * Output JSON:
25:  *   {
26:  *     scriptCompleted: true,
27:  *     stats: { filesScanned, filesWithImports, totalEdges },
28:  *     importMap: { <path>: [<resolvedPath>, ...], ... }
29:  *   }
30:  *
31:  * Logging: stderr only (stdout reserved for piped tools).
32:  * Per-file resilience: failures emit `Warning: extract-import-map: ...` and
33:  * set importMap[path] = [], they do not abort the script.
34:  */
35: 
36: import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
37: import { dirname, resolve, join, posix } from 'node:path';
38: import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
39: import { existsSync, readFileSync, realpathSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
40: import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
41: 
42: /**
43:  * Read a list of files concurrently while preserving result order. Failures
44:  * are returned in-place as `{ raw: null, err }` so callers can emit the same
45:  * per-file warnings they did under the previous sequential `readFileSync`
46:  * loops.
47:  *
48:  * `paths` is a list of `{ key, absPath }` pairs; `key` is whatever the caller
49:  * wants to attach the result to (typically a project-relative POSIX path).
50:  */
51: async function readFilesParallel(paths) {
52:   return Promise.all(
53:     paths.map(async ({ key, absPath }) => {
54:       try {
55:         const raw = await readFile(absPath, 'utf-8');
56:         return { key, raw, err: null };
57:       } catch (err) {
58:         return { key, raw: null, err };
59:       }
60:     }),
61:   );
62: }
63: 
64: const __dirname = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
65: // skills/understand/ -> plugin root is two dirs up
66: const pluginRoot = resolve(__dirname, '../..');
67: const require = createRequire(resolve(pluginRoot, 'package.json'));
68: 
69: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
70: // Resolve @understand-anything/core
71: //
72: // Node ESM dynamic import() requires a file:// URL on Windows; passing a raw
73: // absolute path like "C:\..." throws ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME because the
74: // loader parses "C:" as a URL scheme. Wrap both resolutions in pathToFileURL().
75: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
76: let core;
77: try {
78:   core = await import(pathToFileURL(require.resolve('@understand-anything/core')).href);
79: } catch {
80:   // Fallback: direct path for installed plugin cache layouts
81:   core = await import(pathToFileURL(resolve(pluginRoot, 'packages/core/dist/index.js')).href);
82: }
83: 
84: const { TreeSitterPlugin, PluginRegistry, builtinLanguageConfigs, registerAllParsers } = core;
85: 
86: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
87: // Path helpers
88: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
89: 
90: /**
91:  * Normalize a project-relative path to forward slashes (POSIX). Project-scanner
92:  * always emits forward slashes; we re-normalize to keep this script
93:  * cross-platform.
94:  */
95: function toPosix(p) {
96:   return p.split(/[\\/]/).filter(Boolean).join('/');
97: }
98: 
99: // ECMAScript relational string comparison is lexicographic over UTF-16 code
100: // units, so path ordering is stable across ICU versions, locales, and hosts.
101: function comparePaths(a, b) {
102:   if (a === b) return 0;
103:   return a < b ? -1 : 1;
104: }
105: 
106: /**
107:  * Join a directory with a relative segment, normalizing `.`/`..` segments and
108:  * returning a forward-slash POSIX path. Anchored at project root (no leading
109:  * slash). Returns '' if the path walks above the project root.
110:  */
111: function resolveRelative(dir, rel) {
112:   const parts = (dir ? dir.split('/').filter(Boolean) : []).concat(
113:     rel.split('/').filter(Boolean),
114:   );
115:   const stack = [];
116:   for (const part of parts) {
117:     if (part === '' || part === '.') continue;
118:     if (part === '..') {
119:       if (stack.length === 0) return '';
120:       stack.pop();
121:     } else {
122:       stack.push(part);
123:     }
124:   }
125:   return stack.join('/');
126: }
127: 
128: /**
129:  * Return the directory portion of a project-relative path (no trailing slash,
130:  * '' for top-level files).
131:  */
132: function dirOf(p) {
133:   const i = p.lastIndexOf('/');
134:   return i === -1 ? '' : p.slice(0, i);
135: }

137: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
138: // Config loading
139: //
140: // Cached once at startup. Per-file resolvers consume these values; they MUST
141: // NOT re-read these files (a 1000-file project would otherwise re-parse the
142: // same config 1000 times).
143: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
144: 
145: /**
146:  * Parse a single tsconfig.json file content and return
147:  * `{ baseUrl: string, paths: Map<string, string[]> }` or `null` if both the
148:  * comment-stripped and raw parses fail. Centralizes the "JSONC-then-raw"
149:  * fallback so callers can iterate many tsconfigs without duplicating the
150:  * try/catch ladder.
151:  *
152:  * Returning `null` (rather than throwing) lets the caller emit a Warning:
153:  * with the exact tsconfig path that failed; bubbling the error would
154:  * conceal which file was at fault when many tsconfigs are loaded.
155:  */
156: function parseTsConfigText(raw) {
157:   // tsconfig.json often contains JSONC-style comments; strip line and block
158:   // comments before parsing. The strip is naive (it doesn't honor string
159:   // contents), so we fall back to the raw text on failure.
160:   const stripped = raw
161:     .replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, '')
162:     .replace(/(^|[^:])\/\/.*$/gm, '$1');
163:   let parsed;
164:   try {
165:     parsed = JSON.parse(stripped);
166:   } catch {
167:     try {
168:       parsed = JSON.parse(raw);
169:     } catch {
170:       return null;
171:     }
172:   }
173:   const compilerOptions = parsed?.compilerOptions ?? {};
174:   const baseUrl = compilerOptions.baseUrl ?? '.';
175:   const paths = new Map();
176:   if (compilerOptions.paths && typeof compilerOptions.paths === 'object') {
177:     for (const [alias, targets] of Object.entries(compilerOptions.paths)) {
178:       if (Array.isArray(targets)) {
179:         paths.set(alias, targets);
180:       }
181:     }
182:   }
183:   return { baseUrl, paths };
184: }

186: /**
187:  * Load every `tsconfig.json` discovered in the input file list and parse
188:  * each. Returns `Map<dirPath, { baseUrl, paths }>` keyed by the
189:  * project-relative POSIX directory containing the tsconfig (empty string
190:  * for a root-level tsconfig.json).
191:  *
192:  * `paths` keys keep their trailing `*` wildcards intact (e.g. `"@/*"`); the
193:  * resolver matches them by prefix. Values are arrays because tsconfig
194:  * allows multiple targets per alias.
195:  *
196:  * WHY plural: pnpm/yarn workspace monorepos commonly carry per-package
197:  * tsconfig.json files with package-scoped `paths` aliases. Loading only
198:  * the root tsconfig would (1) miss aliases defined in sub-packages and
199:  * (2) erroneously apply root aliases to files in sub-packages that
200:  * redefine them. Per-importer walk-up is the only correct behavior.
201:  *
202:  * Returns an empty map if no tsconfigs are found — many JS-only projects
203:  * have none, and relative imports still resolve without one. On parse
204:  * failure for a specific tsconfig, emits a Warning: pointing at the bad
205:  * file and skips it (the rest of the project keeps working).
206:  *
207:  * Parse strategy (per-file, in parseTsConfigText):
208:  *   1. Try the comment-stripped text (handles JSONC-style tsconfigs).
209:  *   2. If that fails, retry the ORIGINAL raw text — recovers the case
210:  *      where the stripper damaged a string literal containing `//`.
211:  *   3. If both fail, warn and skip — that tsconfig contributes no aliases.
212:  */
213: async function loadTsConfigs(projectRoot, files) {
214:   const out = new Map();
215:   const warnings = [];
216:   // Collect the candidate paths in the original file order before reading,
217:   // so warning emit order matches the previous sequential implementation.
218:   const candidates = [];
219:   for (const f of files) {
220:     const p = toPosix(f.path);
221:     const base = p.includes('/') ? p.slice(p.lastIndexOf('/') + 1) : p;
222:     if (base !== 'tsconfig.json') continue;
223:     const absPath = join(projectRoot, p);
224:     if (!existsSync(absPath)) continue;
225:     candidates.push({ key: p, absPath });
226:   }
227:   const reads = await readFilesParallel(candidates);
228:   for (const { key: p, raw, err } of reads) {
229:     if (err) {
230:       // absPath isn't carried through the helper return shape; reconstruct it.
231:       warnings.push(
232:         `Warning: extract-import-map: tsconfig.json at ${join(projectRoot, p)} failed ` +
233:         `to read (${err.message}) — path aliases from this config will ` +
234:         `not be applied — relative imports unaffected\n`,
235:       );
236:       continue;
237:     }
238:     const parsed = parseTsConfigText(raw);
239:     if (!parsed) {
240:       warnings.push(
241:         `Warning: extract-import-map: tsconfig.json at ${join(projectRoot, p)} failed ` +
242:         `to parse — path aliases from this config will not be applied ` +
243:         `— relative imports unaffected\n`,
244:       );
245:       continue;
246:     }
247:     out.set(dirOf(p), parsed);
248:   }
249:   return { configs: out, warnings };
250: }

252: /**
253:  * Load every `go.mod` discovered in the input file list and extract its
254:  * `module <name>` line. Returns `Map<dirPath, moduleName>` where `dirPath`
255:  * is the project-relative POSIX directory containing the go.mod (empty
256:  * string for a root-level go.mod).
257:  *
258:  * WHY plural: multi-service / multi-module repositories (e.g. Google's
259:  * microservices-demo) have one go.mod per service. The resolver dispatches
260:  * per importer by walking up to the nearest go.mod, so a single root-only
261:  * lookup misses every file that lives inside a sub-module.
262:  *
263:  * Files outside the discovered `files[]` are ignored — the project-scanner
264:  * is the single source of truth for what the user considers part of the
265:  * project. On read failure for a discovered go.mod we silently skip that
266:  * entry; the per-file resolver will surface the "no ancestor go.mod" warning
267:  * if it matters for any importer.
268:  *
269:  * Example go.mod:
270:  *   module github.com/foo/bar
271:  *   go 1.21
272:  *
273:  * The resolver uses each module's prefix to translate
274:  * `import "github.com/foo/bar/x"` into the project-internal `x/<file>.go`.
275:  */
276: async function loadGoModules(projectRoot, files) {
277:   const out = new Map();
278:   // loadGoModules currently emits no warnings (read failures are silently
279:   // skipped — per-file resolvers surface "no ancestor go.mod" later), but
280:   // the `{ data, warnings }` shape matches loadTsConfigs / loadPhpAutoloads
281:   // so the concurrent caller in buildResolutionContext can drain them
282:   // uniformly in canonical order.
283:   const warnings = [];
284:   const candidates = [];
285:   for (const f of files) {
286:     const p = toPosix(f.path);
287:     const base = p.includes('/') ? p.slice(p.lastIndexOf('/') + 1) : p;
288:     if (base !== 'go.mod') continue;
289:     const absPath = join(projectRoot, p);
290:     if (!existsSync(absPath)) continue;
291:     candidates.push({ key: p, absPath });
292:   }
293:   const reads = await readFilesParallel(candidates);
294:   for (const { key: p, raw, err } of reads) {
295:     if (err) continue;
296:     let moduleName = '';
297:     for (const line of raw.split(/\r?\n/)) {
298:       const trimmed = line.replace(/\/\/.*$/, '').trim();
299:       if (!trimmed.startsWith('module ')) continue;
300:       moduleName = trimmed.slice('module '.length).trim();
301:       break;
302:     }
303:     if (!moduleName) continue;
304:     out.set(dirOf(p), moduleName);
305:   }
306:   return { modules: out, warnings };
307: }

309: /**
310:  * Parse Swift Package.swift target declarations just enough for import-map
311:  * resolution. Swift imports modules, and SwiftPM target names are module names.
312:  * The common convention is `Sources/<Target>`, but packages can override the
313:  * source directory with `path: "..."`; without this light manifest pass those
314:  * custom targets would stay disconnected.
315:  *
316:  * This is intentionally a focused parser, not a Swift evaluator. It handles
317:  * `.target(...)`, `.executableTarget(...)`, and `.testTarget(...)` calls with
318:  * literal `name:` and optional literal `path:` arguments.
319:  */
320: function parseSwiftPackageTargets(raw) {
321:   const targets = [];
322:   const callRe = /\.(target|executableTarget|testTarget)\s*\(/g;
323:   let match;
324: 
325:   while ((match = callRe.exec(raw)) !== null) {
326:     const kind = match[1];
327:     const bodyStart = callRe.lastIndex;
328:     let depth = 1;
329:     let i = bodyStart;
330:     let inString = false;
331:     let quote = '';
332:     let escaped = false;
333: 
334:     for (; i < raw.length; i++) {
335:       const ch = raw[i];
336:       if (inString) {
337:         if (escaped) {
338:           escaped = false;
339:         } else if (ch === '\\') {
340:           escaped = true;
341:         } else if (ch === quote) {
342:           inString = false;
343:         }
344:         continue;
345:       }
346: 
347:       if (ch === '"' || ch === "'") {
348:         inString = true;
349:         quote = ch;
350:         continue;
351:       }
352:       if (ch === '(') depth += 1;
353:       if (ch === ')') {
354:         depth -= 1;
355:         if (depth === 0) break;
356:       }
357:     }
358: 
359:     const body = raw.slice(bodyStart, i);
360:     callRe.lastIndex = i + 1;
361: 
362:     const name = body.match(/\bname\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/)?.[1];
363:     if (!name) continue;
364:     const explicitPath = body.match(/\bpath\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/)?.[1];
365:     const defaultRoot = kind === 'testTarget' ? 'Tests' : 'Sources';
366:     targets.push({
367:       name,
368:       path: explicitPath || `${defaultRoot}/${name}`,
369:     });
370:   }
371: 
372:   return targets;
373: }
374: 
375: async function loadSwiftPackageTargets(projectRoot, files) {
376:   const targets = new Map();
377:   const warnings = [];
378:   const candidates = [];
379: 
380:   for (const f of files) {
381:     const p = toPosix(f.path);
382:     const base = p.includes('/') ? p.slice(p.lastIndexOf('/') + 1) : p;
383:     if (base !== 'Package.swift') continue;
384:     const absPath = join(projectRoot, p);
385:     if (!existsSync(absPath)) continue;
386:     candidates.push({ key: p, absPath });
387:   }
388: 
389:   const reads = await readFilesParallel(candidates);
390:   for (const { key: p, raw, err } of reads) {
391:     if (err) continue;
392:     const packageDir = dirOf(p);
393:     for (const target of parseSwiftPackageTargets(raw)) {
394:       const targetPath = resolveRelative(packageDir, target.path.replace(/\\/g, '/'));
395:       if (!targetPath) continue;
396:       if (!targets.has(target.name)) targets.set(target.name, new Set());
397:       targets.get(target.name).add(targetPath);
398:     }
399:   }
400: 
401:   return { targets, warnings };
402: }
403: 
404: /**
405:  * Walk up from `startDir` (project-relative POSIX, '' for project root)
406:  * and return the DEEPEST ancestor directory that exists as a key in
407:  * `configMap`, or undefined if no ancestor matches.
408:  *
409:  * Determinism: ancestors are inspected from deepest to shallowest, so the
410:  * deepest match is always picked. This matches the way TS/JS / PHP / Go
411:  * tools resolve nearest config in the wild ("nearest enclosing").
412:  *
413:  * Defensive note: if multiple distinct keys somehow share a depth (cannot
414:  * happen with proper directory paths, but a malformed input could), the
415:  * caller is expected to have normalized the keys. We do not re-sort here
416:  * because the iteration order is determined by depth alone.
417:  */
418: function findNearestConfigDir(startDir, configMap) {
419:   if (configMap.size === 0) return undefined;
420:   // Walk ancestors from the importer's directory up to the project root.
421:   // Slicing the parts array gives every prefix; we test each from longest
422:   // to shortest so the deepest match wins.
423:   const parts = startDir ? startDir.split('/').filter(Boolean) : [];
424:   for (let i = parts.length; i >= 0; i--) {
425:     const ancestor = parts.slice(0, i).join('/');
426:     if (configMap.has(ancestor)) return ancestor;
427:   }
428:   return undefined;
429: }

431: /**
432:  * Resolution context shared across all per-file resolver calls. Holds:
433:  *  - fileSet: Set<string> of every input file's posix path
434:  *  - tsConfigs: Map<dir, { baseUrl, paths }> from every tsconfig.json in
435:  *    `files[]`. Per-import resolution walks up from the importer to the
436:  *    nearest enclosing tsconfig.
437:  *  - goModules: Map<dir, moduleName> from every go.mod in `files[]`.
438:  *  - phpAutoloads: Map<dir, autoloadMap> from every composer.json in
439:  *    `files[]`. Resolved paths are anchored at the composer's directory.
440:  *  - goFilesByDir: Map<dir, string[]> of .go files per directory (built
441:  *    once so Go's package-level import dispatch doesn't re-scan the file
442:  *    set per import).
443:  *
444:  * Build once; pass everywhere.
445:  */
446: async function buildResolutionContext(projectRoot, files) {
447:   const fileSet = new Set(files.map(f => toPosix(f.path)));
448: 
449:   // These config-loader passes are independent and each does its own
450:   // batched parallel I/O; run them concurrently so the wait for a slow
451:   // tsconfig.json read doesn't block go.mod / composer.json / SwiftPM scanning.
452:   //
453:   // Each loader BUFFERS warnings into a private array rather than writing
454:   // them to stderr inline. If a loader streamed warnings directly during
455:   // the concurrent passes, lines from independent loader families could
456:   // interleave based on I/O timing — that would break the pre-PR
457:   // deterministic order (ts → go → php → swift) and make stderr-diff verification
458:   // flaky. Drain the buffers in canonical order *after* Promise.all, so
459:   // a fixture with `(malformed tsconfig.json, malformed composer.json)`
460:   // always emits `tsconfig…\ncomposer…\n`, never the reverse.
461:   const [tsResult, goResult, phpResult, swiftResult] = await Promise.all([
462:     loadTsConfigs(projectRoot, files),
463:     loadGoModules(projectRoot, files),
464:     loadPhpAutoloads(projectRoot, files),
465:     loadSwiftPackageTargets(projectRoot, files),
466:   ]);
467:   for (const w of tsResult.warnings) process.stderr.write(w);
468:   for (const w of goResult.warnings) process.stderr.write(w);
469:   for (const w of phpResult.warnings) process.stderr.write(w);
470:   for (const w of swiftResult.warnings) process.stderr.write(w);
471:   const tsConfigs = tsResult.configs;
472:   const goModules = goResult.modules;
473:   const phpAutoloads = phpResult.autoloads;
474: 
475:   // Index .go files by their parent directory so the Go resolver can
476:   // expand a package-level import to all member .go files in O(1).
477:   const goFilesByDir = new Map();
478:   for (const f of files) {
479:     if (!f.path.endsWith('.go')) continue;
480:     const p = toPosix(f.path);
481:     const d = dirOf(p);
482:     if (!goFilesByDir.has(d)) goFilesByDir.set(d, []);
483:     goFilesByDir.get(d).push(p);
484:   }
485:   for (const arr of goFilesByDir.values()) {
486:     arr.sort(comparePaths);
487:   }
488: 
489:   // Build per-extension suffix indices for dotted-FQN resolvers (Java,
490:   // Kotlin, Scala, C#). Indexed once; reused for every import dispatch.
491:   const javaIndex = buildSuffixIndex(files, p => p.endsWith('.java'));
492:   const kotlinIndex = buildSuffixIndex(files, p => p.endsWith('.kt'));
493:   const scalaFilePredicate = p => p.endsWith('.scala') || p.endsWith('.sc');
494:   const scalaIndex = buildSuffixIndex(files, scalaFilePredicate);
495:   const scalaPackageIndex = buildPackageIndex(files, scalaFilePredicate);
496:   const csIndex = buildSuffixIndex(files, p => p.endsWith('.cs'));
497:   const swiftModuleIndex = buildSwiftModuleIndex(files, swiftResult.targets);
498: 
499:   return {
500:     projectRoot,
501:     fileSet,
502:     tsConfigs,
503:     goModules,
504:     goFilesByDir,
505:     javaIndex,
506:     kotlinIndex,
507:     scalaIndex,
508:     scalaPackageIndex,
509:     csIndex,
510:     swiftModuleIndex,
511:     phpAutoloads,
512:     // Dedupe Sets for one-time-per-file warnings. Keyed by importer file
513:     // path. Mutated by resolvers.
514:     _warnedNoRustCrateRoot: new Set(),
515:     _warnedNoGoModule: new Set(),
516:   };
517: }

519: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
520: // TypeScript / JavaScript resolver
521: //
522: // Handles:
523: //   - Relative imports: `import x from './foo'` -> `<dir>/foo` + ext probes
524: //   - tsconfig path aliases: `import x from '@/foo'` -> `<baseUrl>/<target>/foo`
525: //
526: // `imp.source` from tree-sitter is the literal string content of the import
527: // path (no quotes). We don't need to redo the regex work — we just classify
528: // the source string and dispatch.
529: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
530: 
531: // Extensions probed when the import has no extension. The order mirrors the
532: // historical project-scanner prose so behavior matches existing fixtures.
533: const TS_EXT_PROBES = [
534:   '.ts', '.tsx', '.js', '.jsx', '.mjs', '.cjs',
535:   '/index.ts', '/index.tsx', '/index.js', '/index.jsx',
536: ];
537: 
538: /**
539:  * NodeNext / Node16 / Bundler-with-explicit-extensions ESM TypeScript convention:
540:  * TypeScript does NOT rewrite import specifiers during compilation, so source
541:  * files import their COMPILED specifier (`./config.js`) even when only
542:  * `./config.ts` exists on disk. We map each compiled-output extension to the
543:  * TS source extensions that could have produced it, in priority order.
544:  *
545:  * Without this rewrite, ESM-TS projects (which is now the default for any new
546:  * TS project) end up with a near-edgeless knowledge graph because every
547:  * project-internal import fails to resolve. (#294)
548:  */
549: const NODENEXT_REWRITES = {
550:   '.js': ['.ts', '.tsx', '.js', '.jsx'],
551:   '.jsx': ['.tsx', '.jsx'],
552:   '.mjs': ['.mts', '.mjs', '.ts'],
553:   '.cjs': ['.cts', '.cjs', '.ts'],
554: };
555: 
556: /**
557:  * Try ext probes against the file set for the given base path. Returns the
558:  * first matching project-relative path, or null. If the base path already has
559:  * a code extension AND exists in the file set, returns it directly.
560:  *
561:  * For NodeNext-style imports (`./foo.js` where only `./foo.ts` exists), apply
562:  * the source-extension rewrite — see NODENEXT_REWRITES above.
563:  */
564: function probeWithExtensions(basePath, fileSet) {
565:   if (!basePath) return null;
566:   // Exact match (import already had an extension that resolves on disk)
567:   if (fileSet.has(basePath)) return basePath;
568: 
569:   // NodeNext rewrite: if the basePath ends with a compiled-output extension
570:   // but no such file exists, try the corresponding source extensions. We do
571:   // this BEFORE the legacy "append extensions" loop because for an import
572:   // like `./foo.js`, appending `.ts` would produce `foo.js.ts` (always wrong)
573:   // while the correct candidate is `foo.ts`.
574:   for (const [outExt, srcExts] of Object.entries(NODENEXT_REWRITES)) {
575:     if (!basePath.endsWith(outExt)) continue;
576:     const stem = basePath.slice(0, -outExt.length);
577:     for (const srcExt of srcExts) {
578:       const candidate = stem + srcExt;
579:       if (fileSet.has(candidate)) return candidate;
580:     }
581:     // The basePath had an explicit compiled extension — don't fall through
582:     // to the "append extensions" loop, which would produce nonsense like
583:     // `foo.js.ts`. If NodeNext rewrite didn't find anything, return null.
584:     return null;
585:   }
586: 
587:   for (const ext of TS_EXT_PROBES) {
588:     const candidate = basePath + ext;
589:     if (fileSet.has(candidate)) return candidate;
590:   }
591:   return null;
592: }
593: 
594: /**
595:  * Resolve a TypeScript / JavaScript import. Returns project-relative resolved
596:  * path or null. External packages return null.
597:  *
598:  * Path-alias resolution walks up from the importer's directory to find the
599:  * nearest enclosing tsconfig.json (monorepo-friendly). `baseUrl`-relative
600:  * targets are anchored at THAT tsconfig's directory, matching the way the
601:  * TypeScript compiler resolves nested project configs.
602:  */
603: export function resolveTsJsImport(rawImport, file, ctx) {
604:   if (!rawImport || typeof rawImport !== 'string') return null;
605:   const src = rawImport.trim();
606:   if (!src) return null;
607: 
608:   const importerDir = dirOf(toPosix(file.path));
609: 
610:   // Relative imports: ./foo, ../foo — tsconfig has no bearing here.
611:   if (src.startsWith('./') || src.startsWith('../')) {
612:     const base = resolveRelative(importerDir, src);
613:     return probeWithExtensions(base, ctx.fileSet);
614:   }
615: 
616:   // tsconfig path aliases. Walk up from the importer to find the nearest
617:   // tsconfig.json; resolve targets relative to THAT tsconfig's directory.
618:   // Without the walk-up, a root tsconfig would either swallow aliases that
619:   // belong to a sub-package or fail to apply sub-package-defined aliases.
620:   const tsConfigDir = findNearestConfigDir(importerDir, ctx.tsConfigs);
621:   if (tsConfigDir !== undefined) {
622:     const tsConfig = ctx.tsConfigs.get(tsConfigDir);
623:     const { baseUrl, paths } = tsConfig;
624:     if (paths && paths.size > 0) {
625:       for (const [alias, targets] of paths) {
626:         const aliasMatch = matchTsAlias(alias, src);
627:         if (aliasMatch === null) continue;
628:         for (const target of targets) {
629:           const mapped = applyTsAlias(target, aliasMatch);
630:           // baseUrl is tsconfig-dir-relative; '.', './', '' all mean the
631:           // tsconfig's own directory. We anchor at tsConfigDir so a nested
632:           // tsconfig's `baseUrl: '.'` maps to its package, not project root.
633:           const normalizedBase = baseUrl === '.' || baseUrl === ''
634:             ? ''
635:             : toPosix(baseUrl);
636:           const relativeToConfig = normalizedBase
637:             ? posix.join(normalizedBase, mapped)
638:             : mapped;
639:           // posix.normalize strips a leading "./" left over when both
640:           // tsConfigDir and normalizedBase are empty (root tsconfig with
641:           // `"@/*": ["./*"]`, the create-next-app default). Without this the

644:           const candidate = posix.normalize(

647:               : relativeToConfig,
648:           );

650:           if (candidate.startsWith('..')) continue;

662: /**
663:  * Match an import against a tsconfig paths alias. Aliases use `*` as a single

673:   const prefix = alias.slice(0, starIdx);
674:   const suffix = alias.slice(starIdx + 1);

676:   if (!src.endsWith(suffix)) return null;

678:   if (src.length < prefix.length + suffix.length) return null;
679:   return src.slice(prefix.length, src.length - suffix.length);

684:  * matchTsAlias — if the target has no `*`, return it as-is (rare, but valid).

692: /**
693:  * Tree-sitter's TS/JS extractor only records ES module `import` declarations.

697:  * content — we only want literal string arguments, so the regex is narrow.

699:  * Limitations (intentional):
700:  *   - Computed requires (`require(name)`) are external/dynamic — skipped.
701:  *   - Template-literal requires are unresolved.
702:  *   - String concatenation in the argument is unresolved.

706: /**
707:  * Strip JS/TS line and block comments before running text-pattern matchers.

720: function extractRequireSources(content) {

722:   let m;
723:   const stripped = stripJsLikeComments(content);

725:   while ((m = REQUIRE_LITERAL_RE.exec(stripped)) !== null) {
726:     sources.push(m[2]);
727:   }
728:   return sources;
729: }

731: /**
732:  * Kotlin has no tree-sitter extractor in this project, so we collect its
733:  * import sources via a focused regex pass. Kotlin imports are syntactically
734:  * simple: one per line, `import x.y.Z` or `import x.y.Z as Alias` (or
735:  * `import x.y.*` for star imports). We capture the dotted FQN and let the
736:  * dotted resolver classify wildcards.

738:  * The capture is a strict qualifiedName grammar — a leading identifier
739:  * followed by zero or more `.identifier` segments and an optional trailing
740:  * `.*` for star-imports. The looser `[\w.*]+` form previously here would
741:  * match pathological inputs like `import ...` or `import .foo`.

747:   const sources = [];
748:   let m;
749:   KOTLIN_IMPORT_RE.lastIndex = 0;
750:   while ((m = KOTLIN_IMPORT_RE.exec(content)) !== null) {
751:     sources.push(m[1]);
752:   }
753:   return sources;
754: }

756: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
757: // Python resolver
758: //
759: // Tree-sitter's Python extractor emits one entry per import statement:
760: //   - `import a.b.c`          -> { source: 'a.b.c', specifiers: ['a.b.c'] }
761: //   - `from a.b.c import x,y` -> { source: 'a.b.c', specifiers: ['x','y'] }
762: //   - `from . import x`       -> { source: '', specifiers: ['x'] }
763: //   - `from .x import y`      -> { source: '.x', specifiers: ['y'] }
764: //   - `from ..pkg import y`   -> { source: '..pkg', specifiers: ['y'] }
765: //
766: // We can't tell relative from absolute by the source string alone — the dots
767: // could be a leading-dot relative source OR a literal `.` package separator.
768: // Python's lexical convention disambiguates: leading dots ALWAYS mean
769: // relative. Tree-sitter preserves leading dots verbatim in the source field,
770: // so we can dispatch on the prefix.
771: //
772: // Resolution rules:
773: //   1. Relative (starts with `.`): walk up parent dirs by leading-dot count,
774: //      then descend by the remaining dotted segments.
775: //   2. Absolute (no leading dot): walk up from the importer's directory,
776: //      trying EACH ancestor as a candidate Python root. The first ancestor
777: //      under which probing succeeds wins. This matches how multi-service
778: //      Python repos work in practice — each service directory acts as its
779: //      own root for unqualified `import sibling` style imports
780: //      (e.g. microservices-demo's per-service grpc stubs).
781: //
782: //      We don't gate this on setup.py / pyproject.toml detection. The
783: //      probe itself IS the test of whether the ancestor is a candidate
784: //      root: an absent module just continues the walk. The closest
785: //      ancestor where the import resolves wins, which gives importer
786: //      scope precedence (sibling files override remote candidates).
787: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
788: 
789: /**
790:  * Resolve a Python import. Unlike most resolvers this can produce multiple
791:  * matches (one for the package `__init__.py` plus one per submodule
792:  * specifier), so the signature differs: returns string[].
793:  *
794:  * Returns empty array for external/unresolved packages.
795:  */
796: export function resolvePythonImport(rawImport, specifiers, file, ctx) {
797:   if (typeof rawImport !== 'string') return [];
798:   const src = rawImport;
799:   const importerDir = dirOf(toPosix(file.path));
800: 
801:   // Count leading dots; the rest is a dotted module path
802:   let dots = 0;
803:   while (dots < src.length && src.charCodeAt(dots) === 0x2e /* '.' */) dots++;
804:   const tail = src.slice(dots);
805:   const tailSegments = tail ? tail.split('.').filter(Boolean) : [];
806: 
807:   if (dots > 0) {
808:     // Relative import. `from . import x` (dots=1, tail='') walks up zero
809:     // directories (sibling level); `from .. import x` walks up one.
810:     // Relative imports are anchored at the importer's package, so we do
811:     // NOT do the per-root walk-up here — leading dots already encode the
812:     // exact anchor.
813:     const importerParts = importerDir ? importerDir.split('/').filter(Boolean) : [];
814:     const dropLevels = dots - 1;
815:     if (dropLevels > importerParts.length) {
816:       // Walked above the project root — unresolvable
817:       return [];
818:     }
819:     const baseParts = importerParts.slice(0, importerParts.length - dropLevels);
820: 
821:     // `from .[..] import x, y` with no dotted tail — specifiers are siblings
822:     // at `baseParts`. Probe directly without requiring `<baseParts>/__init__.py`
823:     // to exist: PEP 328 implicit namespace packages are common in modern
824:     // Python (no `__init__.py`), and `resolvePythonProbe` would otherwise
825:     // gate specifier resolution on the package marker and drop these imports.
826:     if (tailSegments.length === 0) {
827:       if (!Array.isArray(specifiers) || specifiers.length === 0) return [];
828:       const base = baseParts.join('/');
829:       const matches = [];
830:       for (const spec of specifiers) {
831:         // Wildcard `*` and qualified specifiers (`Foo.bar`) skip; the
832:         // surface name is what tree-sitter records for `from . import x`.
833:         if (!spec || spec === '*' || spec.includes('.')) continue;
834:         const subFile = base ? `${base}/${spec}.py` : `${spec}.py`;
835:         const subInit = base ? `${base}/${spec}/__init__.py` : `${spec}/__init__.py`;
836:         if (ctx.fileSet.has(subFile)) matches.push(subFile);
837:         else if (ctx.fileSet.has(subInit)) matches.push(subInit);
838:       }
839:       return matches;
840:     }
841: 
842:     const moduleParts = baseParts.concat(tailSegments);
843:     return resolvePythonProbe(moduleParts, specifiers, ctx);
844:   }
845: 
846:   // Absolute import. Walk up from the importer's directory and try every
847:   // ancestor as a candidate Python root — the first one where probing
848:   // resolves anything wins. This handles the multi-service / multi-package
849:   // case where each service's directory acts as its own implicit
850:   // sys.path entry (e.g. `import demo_pb2_grpc` from
851:   // `src/emailservice/email_server.py` should resolve to
852:   // `src/emailservice/demo_pb2_grpc.py`, NOT fail because the file isn't
853:   // at `<projectRoot>/demo_pb2_grpc.py`).
854:   //
855:   // Importer-scope precedence (deepest ancestor first) means that when
856:   // the same module name exists in multiple services, each service's
857:   // file shadows the others — no cross-service edges.
858:   if (tailSegments.length === 0) {
859:     // `from . import x` is dots>0 only; reaching here means the source
860:     // was the empty string. Nothing to probe.
861:     return [];
862:   }
863: 
864:   const importerParts = importerDir ? importerDir.split('/').filter(Boolean) : [];
865:   for (let i = importerParts.length; i >= 0; i--) {
866:     const rootParts = importerParts.slice(0, i);
867:     const candidateModule = rootParts.concat(tailSegments);
868:     const matches = resolvePythonProbe(candidateModule, specifiers, ctx);
869:     if (matches.length > 0) return matches;
870:   }
871:   return [];
872: }

874: /**
875:  * Given a fully-qualified module-path segment list (e.g. ['src','utils']),
876:  * probe the file set for `a/b/c.py` then `a/b/c/__init__.py`. On package
877:  * match, also probe each specifier as a submodule. Returns an array of
878:  * resolved project-relative paths (deduped by Set in caller).
879:  */
880: function resolvePythonProbe(moduleParts, specifiers, ctx) {
881:   if (moduleParts.length === 0) {
882:     // `from . import x` case: importer's package is the implicit module;
883:     // each x is a sibling module to probe directly.
884:     return [];
885:   }
886:   const base = moduleParts.join('/');
887:   const matches = [];
888: 
889:   const moduleFile = `${base}.py`;
890:   const packageInit = `${base}/__init__.py`;
891: 
892:   if (ctx.fileSet.has(moduleFile)) {
893:     matches.push(moduleFile);
894:     return matches; // No further probing on a leaf module file.
895:   }
896:   if (ctx.fileSet.has(packageInit)) {
897:     matches.push(packageInit);
898:     // Package match: probe each specifier as a submodule
899:     if (Array.isArray(specifiers)) {
900:       for (const spec of specifiers) {
901:         // Wildcard `*` and qualified specifiers (`Foo.bar`) skip; the
902:         // surface name is what tree-sitter records for `from pkg import x`.
903:         if (!spec || spec === '*' || spec.includes('.')) continue;
904:         const subFile = `${base}/${spec}.py`;
905:         const subInit = `${base}/${spec}/__init__.py`;
906:         if (ctx.fileSet.has(subFile)) matches.push(subFile);
907:         else if (ctx.fileSet.has(subInit)) matches.push(subInit);
908:       }
909:     }
910:     return matches;
911:   }
912: 
913:   // No match — external package.
914:   return [];
915: }

917: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
918: // Go resolver
919: //
920: // Tree-sitter's Go extractor emits the literal import path (without quotes).
921: // Resolution: walk up from the importer's directory to find the nearest
922: // enclosing `go.mod` (multi-module monorepos are the norm). Strip that
923: // module's prefix; the remainder maps to a directory RELATIVE TO THAT
924: // MODULE'S DIRECTORY in the project. Go imports are package-level (not
925: // file-level), so a single `import "github.com/foo/bar/util"` produces edges
926: // to every .go file inside that module's `util/`.
927: //
928: // Cross-module imports (`github.com/foo/bar/X` from a file under a module
929: // that declares `github.com/foo/baz`) are correctly classified as external —
930: // they refer to a different Go module, which from this module's perspective
931: // is a third-party dependency.
932: //
933: // Inputs:
934: //   - rawImport: 'github.com/foo/bar/util' (no quotes)
935: //   - file.path: importer's project-relative path
936: //   - ctx.goModules: Map<dir, moduleName> of every go.mod discovered.
937: //
938: // Result: array of every `<moduleDir>/util/*.go` path in the project
939: // (deduped by caller).
940: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
941: 
942: export function resolveGoImport(rawImport, file, ctx) {
943:   if (!rawImport || typeof rawImport !== 'string') return [];
944:   const src = rawImport.trim();
945:   if (!src) return [];
946: 
947:   const importerPath = toPosix(file.path);
948:   const importerDir = dirOf(importerPath);
949: 
950:   const nearestModuleDir = findNearestConfigDir(importerDir, ctx.goModules);
951:   if (nearestModuleDir === undefined) {
952:     // Warn once per importer file — a single .go file can import several
953:     // module-prefixed paths, so suppress duplicates.
954:     if (!ctx._warnedNoGoModule.has(importerPath)) {
955:       ctx._warnedNoGoModule.add(importerPath);
956:       process.stderr.write(
957:         `Warning: extract-import-map: Go file ${importerPath} has no ` +
958:         `ancestor go.mod — import ${src} unresolvable — module-prefix ` +
959:         `imports skipped\n`,
960:       );
961:     }
962:     return [];
963:   }
964: 
965:   const moduleName = ctx.goModules.get(nearestModuleDir);
966: 
967:   // Strip module prefix; require a `/` boundary so 'githubXcom...' does not
968:   // accidentally match 'github.com...'.
969:   let remainder;
970:   if (src === moduleName) {
971:     remainder = '';
972:   } else if (src.startsWith(moduleName + '/')) {
973:     remainder = src.slice(moduleName.length + 1);
974:   } else {
975:     // External package (stdlib, 3rd-party module, OR a different in-tree
976:     // module — the latter is intentional: from this module's perspective,
977:     // a sibling module is an external dependency).
978:     return [];
979:   }
980: 
981:   // Map to a directory in the project (POSIX style). Anchor at the module's
982:   // own directory, so a sub-module's `<module>/sub` resolves under that
983:   // module's tree rather than under project root.
984:   const subDir = toPosix(remainder);
985:   const targetDir = nearestModuleDir
986:     ? (subDir ? `${nearestModuleDir}/${subDir}` : nearestModuleDir)
987:     : subDir;
988:   const files = ctx.goFilesByDir.get(targetDir);
989:   return files ? [...files] : [];
990: }

992: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
993: // Dotted-package resolver (Java / Kotlin / C#)
994: //
995: // Shared logic: an import like `com.example.foo.Bar` maps to a file
996: // `**/com/example/foo/Bar.<ext>` in the project. Many JVM/CLR projects nest
997: // sources under `src/main/java/`, `src/main/kotlin/`, etc., so the resolver
998: // must search for any file whose suffix matches the dotted-path-as-file form.
999: //
1000: // We pre-build an index: trailing-slash-suffix -> matching project paths.
1001: // Indexing once is O(files * average_segments); per-import lookup is then
1002: // effectively O(1) hash lookup + scan of the bucket.
1003: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1004: 
1005: /**
1006:  * Build an index of all files for a given extension, keyed by their
1007:  * "package-path suffix" form. For each file `src/main/java/com/x/Y.java`,
1008:  * the index gets entries for every suffix that ends at a `/`:
1009:  *   - 'com/x/Y.java'
1010:  *   - 'x/Y.java'
1011:  *   - 'Y.java'
1012:  * keyed off each successively-shorter suffix.
1013:  *
1014:  * Using a Map<suffix, string[]> avoids per-import full table scans; a 50K-file
1015:  * monorepo with deep package nesting still resolves O(1) per import.
1016:  */
1017: function buildSuffixIndex(files, extPredicate) {
1018:   const idx = new Map();
1019:   for (const f of files) {
1020:     const p = toPosix(f.path);
1021:     if (!extPredicate(p)) continue;
1022:     // Generate every "directory-bounded suffix" of the path
1023:     const parts = p.split('/');
1024:     for (let i = 0; i < parts.length; i++) {
1025:       const suffix = parts.slice(i).join('/');
1026:       if (!idx.has(suffix)) idx.set(suffix, []);
1027:       idx.get(suffix).push(p);
1028:     }
1029:   }
1030:   // Deterministic order within each bucket
1031:   for (const arr of idx.values()) {
1032:     arr.sort(comparePaths);
1033:   }
1034:   return idx;
1035: }
1036: 
1037: function buildPackageIndex(files, extPredicate) {
1038:   const idx = new Map();
1039:   for (const f of files) {
1040:     const p = toPosix(f.path);
1041:     if (!extPredicate(p)) continue;
1042:     const dir = dirOf(p);
1043:     if (!dir) continue;
1044: 
1045:     const parts = dir.split('/');
1046:     for (let i = 0; i < parts.length; i++) {
1047:       const suffix = parts.slice(i).join('/');
1048:       if (!idx.has(suffix)) idx.set(suffix, []);
1049:       idx.get(suffix).push(p);
1050:     }
1051:   }
1052:   for (const arr of idx.values()) {
1053:     arr.sort(comparePaths);
1054:   }
1055:   return idx;
1056: }

1058: const SWIFT_SOURCE_ROOT_DIRS = new Set(['source', 'sources', 'test', 'tests']);
1059: const SWIFT_MODULE_CONTAINER_DIRS = new Set([
1060:   'framework',
1061:   'frameworks',
1062:   'library',
1063:   'libraries',
1064:   'module',
1065:   'modules',
1066: ]);

1068: function addSwiftModuleFile(index, moduleName, filePath) {
1069:   if (!moduleName) return;
1070:   if (!/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/.test(moduleName)) return;
1071:   if (!index.has(moduleName)) index.set(moduleName, new Set());
1072:   index.get(moduleName).add(filePath);

1075: function inferSwiftModulesFromPath(filePath) {
1076:   const parts = filePath.split('/');
1077:   const dirs = parts.slice(0, -1);
1078:   const modules = new Set();
1079: 
1080:   for (let i = 0; i < dirs.length - 1; i++) {
1081:     const lower = dirs[i].toLowerCase();
1082:     if (
1083:       SWIFT_SOURCE_ROOT_DIRS.has(lower) ||
1084:       SWIFT_MODULE_CONTAINER_DIRS.has(lower)
1085:     ) {
1086:       modules.add(dirs[i + 1]);
1087:     }
1088:   }
1089: 
1090:   if (dirs.length > 0 && !SWIFT_SOURCE_ROOT_DIRS.has(dirs[0].toLowerCase())) {
1091:     modules.add(dirs[0]);
1092:   }
1093:

1097: /**
1098:  * Build a Swift module-name -> files index.

1100:  * Swift files in the same module do not import each other by relative path;
1101:  * `import Foo` imports a module. We therefore resolve to every project Swift
1102:  * file that belongs to module `Foo`, mirroring the Go resolver's package-level
1103:  * expansion. The index combines SwiftPM manifest targets with common on-disk
1104:  * conventions (`Sources/Foo`, `Tests/FooTests`, and top-level Xcode groups).
1105:  */

1107:   const idx = new Map();
1108:   const targetEntries = [...packageTargets.entries()].map(([name, paths]) => [
1109:     name,
1110:     [...paths].sort(comparePaths),
1111:   ]);

1113:   for (const f of files) {
1114:     const p = toPosix(f.path);
1115:     if (!p.endsWith('.swift')) continue;
1116:     if (p.endsWith('/Package.swift') || p === 'Package.swift') continue;
1117: 
1118:     for (const [moduleName, targetPaths] of targetEntries) {
1119:       for (const targetPath of targetPaths) {
1120:         if (p === targetPath || p.startsWith(`${targetPath}/`)) {
1121:           addSwiftModuleFile(idx, moduleName, p);

1123:       }
1124:     }
1125: 
1126:     for (const moduleName of inferSwiftModulesFromPath(p)) {
1127:       addSwiftModuleFile(idx, moduleName, p);
1128:     }
1129:   }
1130: 
1131:   const out = new Map();
1132:   for (const [moduleName, paths] of idx.entries()) {
1133:     out.set(moduleName, [...paths].sort(comparePaths));
1134:   }
1135:   return out;
1136: }

1138: /**
1139:  * Resolve a dotted-import to a file. `fqn` is the qualified name
1140:  * (`com.example.Foo`); `ext` is the file extension to probe (`.java`,

1143:  * single-file resolution for wildcards, so we drop them. (Tree-sitter
1144:  * already exposes `*` as a specifier; the source field strips it.)

1146:  * Returns array (most cases: 0 or 1 match; multiple if the same suffix
1147:  * appears in multiple source roots).

1150:   if (!fqn || typeof fqn !== 'string') return [];

1152:   const trimmed = fqn.replace(/\.\*$/, '');
1153:   if (!trimmed) return [];
1154:   const filePart = trimmed.replace(/\./g, '/') + ext;
1155:   const matches = suffixIndex.get(filePart);
1156:   return matches ? [...matches] : [];
1157: }

 * extract-import-map.mjs

 * then applies language-specific resolution rules to map them to
 * project-internal file paths.

 * Replaces the LLM-written prose import resolver in agents/project-scanner.md
 * (the prose previously described patterns by language; runtime LLMs produced
 * inconsistent, regex-only scripts with sparse coverage).

 *   node extract-import-map.mjs <input.json> <output.json>

 * Input JSON:

 *     projectRoot: <abs-path>,
